title: GOP Sounding the Alarm Over Massive $200 Million Rescue Mission for Ken Paxton in Texas
snippet: Top Republican strategists are in a state of panic as the cost to defend Ken Paxton’s Texas Senate seat threatens to drain resources from other key battleground races across the country.
content:
WASHINGTON — Senior Republicans are growing increasingly frantic as the price tag to save Texas Senate nominee Ken Paxton tops an unprecedented $200 million, threatening to drain crucial resources away from key battlegrounds in the final stretch of the election cycle.

In private discussions over recent weeks, party officials and veteran Capitol Hill operatives have been pressing Donald Trump’s political team to step up spending in Texas before the window closes. Panic escalated after leaked audio captured Paxton criticizing a recent Trump convention in Dallas, stoking fears that the main pro-Trump super PAC, MAGA Inc., might hesitate to extend its advertising buys beyond mid-October.

A 'Five-Alarm Fire' in Deep-Red Territory

While MAGA Inc. recently increased its commitment to roughly $45 million through October 12, campaign insiders say the group remains undecided on how much more to inject in the home stretch. Meanwhile, the Senate Leadership Fund (SLF)—the primary super PAC aligned with Senate Republican leadership—flooded Texas with an additional $60 million, raising its total investment in the state to a staggering $131 million.

"It’s a five-alarm fire, no doubt," one Republican senator admitted on condition of anonymity to speak candidly about the race. "This is a slow-moving car crash... and there's a 75% chance that the ultimate result here will be catastrophic from a GOP Senate majority standpoint."

The race has tightened significantly as national Democrats ramp up support for their nominee, James Talarico, who had previously lagged in outside spending. Most recent public polling shows Talarico holding a slim lead, though an internal poll released by Paxton’s campaign showed the Republican ahead by three points.

Spillover Concerns for Other Senate Maps

The gargantuan expenditure in traditionally safe Texas is raising red flags for party strategists, who worry the drain on capital will leave candidate funds depleted in toss-up states like Michigan, New Hampshire, Ohio, and North Carolina.

Trump himself acknowledged the growing anxiety at a recent rally, telling supporters, "We’re worried about Michigan. We’re worried about Texas. We’re worried about a few states." Despite describing Paxton as "a pain in the ass sometimes," Trump emphasized his long-standing loyalty as he prepares for an upcoming rally in San Antonio.

Still, GOP operatives in rival swing states argue that sinking over $200 million into a Texas defense is an unforced error driven by Paxton's campaign missteps. "We're focusing so much on Texas—we've never had a problem in Texas," complained one Republican operative tied to a battleground race. "Let's focus on taking back seats we haven't had in years."
